summary:
Base 67 is a 2D mobile offline game built with Flutter. Kids 10-15 years old command a 4-person Mars outpost. Rather than trying to deal with all of the systems at once, players progress through levels that each add one situation a crew has to deal with: power, dust storms, air, radiation, and food and water, culminating in a Commander level that combines them. At each level new information is unlocked, a challenge to use it and a badge. Completing the program earns a Junior Astronaut certificate.
It rises to the challenge by allowing students to experience real mission trade-offs. Power, air, water, food and radiation all have one budget, so every choice helps one system and strains another. Site and hazard values are based on NASA data including Curiosity RAD radiation measurements and SWIM subsurface ice maps. What is real, derived or simplified is labelled in the game.
That’s important because space STEM for kids is often too easy or too hard. It works offline so any kid with a phone can train like an astronaut. Learning one situation at a time builds understanding without confusion.
details:
WHAT IT DOES: BASE 67 is a single-player Android game where you’re a junior astronaut crew building a Mars settlement. Players create and name four crew members, build and repair facilities, manage power, oxygen, water and food, and complete 15 missions in five chapters. Missions are for dust storms, radiation, water ice, greenhouse and crew care. Each mission concludes with a debrief that explains what happened and why. Unlock NASA reference cards in a notebook, badges, and a personalised completion certificate for missions completed.

HOW DOES IT WORK: The deterministic simulation engine drives the base resources, power, events and timers. The mission rules, crew and levels are defined in bundled JSON data files. Each NASA number is read from a NASA data file (never typed into code) by fact id and labelled NASA DATA, GAME VALUE or DERIVED. A data validator checks the original data pack and progress is saved locally on the device.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT Kids learn real facts about Mars while practicing mission planning, resource trade-offs and teamwork. No internet connection is needed, no internet permission is requested, so it can be used everywhere.

TOOLS: Flutter and dart (Android) provider, shared_preferences, crypto. * All visuals are painted in code (CustomPainter) "data": { } JSON Developed with the assistance of AI code helpers (Claude, GitHub Copilot and Codex).

CREATIVITY: Real NASA science that leads to game-like decisions. “Clear data labels separate real science from game design.” Players build their own crew and base and as missions are completed the map shows the settlement expanding.

FACTORS WE EVALUATED: Readability (ages 7-12) and child-friendly content, offline use, accessibility (reduced-motion setting, large-text support, color-blind-safe markers), data accuracy and traceable sources, no NASA logos or branding, and fair, non-punishing progression.
